thread:
Priya (CS): MercuryRetail just asked for a short-term EU capacity bump + IP allowlist. They're reporting <500ms tail latency spikes and said renewal discussion next Thursday is contingent on a stable demo. Can we get a temporary config today?

Priya (CS): Customer details:
- Org: MercuryRetail
- App: Storefront Search (embedding + generation calls)
- Current per-org QPS: 12
- Requested temp QPS: 60 (48h window)
- Region: eu-west-1 preferred (EU latency matters)
- IPs to allowlist (customer provided): `203.0.113.45`, `203.0.113.46` and CIDR `203.0.113.0/29`
- Start: ASAP, End: 2026-03-26T18:00Z

Priya (CS): They also asked for a short-term increase to the per-route burst window (to avoid 429s during demo spikes).

Mike (NetOps): Can we route those requests to the eu edge pool? Any peering gaps with their ISP?

Priya (CS): Mercury says they peer with AWS eu-west-1 and will come from those IPs; they also offered to open a support ticket on their side if we need peering info.

Jamie (SRE): We can do a conservative approach: create a temp rate-profile `mercury_temp_60` scoped to org-id `org_merc_002` + allowlist the CIDR. Canary to two eu hosts for 10m then full rollout. I estimate ~15-25m to apply and validate. I'll need the exact org ID and the desired per-route burst config (tokens/sec or qps).

Priya (CS): Org ID is `org_merc_002`. For burst, customer requested 5x normal window — current window is 100 requests/60s; they want 500/60s for demo.

Mike (NetOps): Confirmed eu edge pool has capacity headroom. Need a firewall rule add for the CIDR on the ingress layer and an ACL entry in our edge proxies. I can push ACL once Jamie gives the temp profile name. ETA 10m after Jamie gives name.

Jamie (SRE): OK creating profile now. Config I'll apply: 
```json
{
  "org_id": "org_merc_002",
  "profile_name": "mercury_temp_60",
  "qps": 60,
  "burst_window": { "requests": 500, "per_seconds": 60 },
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "allowlist": ["203.0.113.45", "203.0.113.46", "203.0.113.0/29"],
  "ttl": "48h"
}
```

Jamie (SRE): Applying to canary hosts now. I'll tail logs for 15m and watch 429/latency metrics.

Ethan (Support): I'll ping the Mercury account team and tell them ETA ~30m. Also will remind them to send a link to their demo timing so we can align rollback.

Lina (Product): Marking this as high renewal risk in the tracker. If this goes well, we should capture the latency numbers and put in their renewal brief.

Mike (NetOps): ACL and firewall rules queued. Pushing to edge proxies in 5m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rate-profile `mercury_temp_60` created and canary applied to hosts eu-edge-03 and eu-edge-07 by Jamie at 2026-03-25T15:34:12Z :white_check_mark:

Jamie (SRE): Canary looks good — no 429s, p95 latency improved slightly under heavier load from test harness. Rolling to full eu pool now. Monitoring for 30m.

Mike (NetOps): ACL added: `allow 203.0.113.0/29` on edge-ingress-eu; firewall rule pushed.

Ethan (Support): Mercury notified. They replied "thanks — seeing smoother responses, big help for demo" :tada:

Lina (Product): Great. Priya, please attach the demo time and any recorded metrics to the renewal ticket. We'll follow up with a short enablement runbook (how we handled the bump + how to request in future).

Priya (CS): Will do. Plan to auto-revoke profile at TTL expiry but also set a manual reminder to confirm rollback at 2026-03-26T18:10Z.

Jamie (SRE): Manual rollback command (if needed):
```bash
# remove temp rate profile
redwoodctl rate-profiles delete --org org_merc_002 mercury_temp_60
# revoke allowlist
redwoodctl network acl remove --region eu-west-1 --cidr 203.0.113.0/29
```

Priya (CS): Thanks team. Leaving this thread open until we confirm full rollback. :thumbsup:
